clue.text: Dull, not married, longed to be in a relationship

indicators.note: married is abbreviated to a single letter in lists, and 'not' asks for that letter to be dropped from the word before

parts.note: matt describes a dull, non-glossy finish
M is the standard abbreviation for married
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A bored single person yearned for a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt is the dull, non-shiny finish of paint or photo paper; M for married is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attached is romantically committed to a partner, the everyday sense of being spoken for.

clue.text: Tourist, initially with bundle, led astray? That's nonsense

indicators.note: something led astray wanders off its proper course, so the letters wander out of order
initially points to only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of the word
a wad is a bundle, as of banknotes
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist carrying a bundle was misled, and someone dismisses the tale as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins T to WAD; 'led' is both fodder and part of the surface phrase 'led astray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, trivial talk or writing, a direct synonym for rubbish of that kind.

clue.text: One under influence, just about consumed with love

indicators.note: the word for just about has swallowed the next piece, holding it within
in a down entry, a piece placed under another comes after it, so the one-letter piece goes second

parts.note: to affect is to influence
Roman numeral one; in a down clue it sits under the previous piece
only means just, as in 'just a few'; 'about' tells it to go round
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: Someone under the influence, nearly overwhelmed by romantic feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' does double duty in the surface sense of overwhelmed, yet it supplies letters and also signals the wrapping; 'about' only tells the just word to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with love is doing it fondly and tenderly, which the adverb describes.

clue.text: Herald getting hot and bothered bearing first of reports

indicators.note: something bothered is agitated and disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the seven letters rearranged

indicators.note: first of asks for just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A town crier flustered by the heat, carrying early news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like 'carrying' but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger announces or signals what is coming, just as a herald proclaims news ahead of an arrival.

clue.text: Cheats held up essential cases

indicators.note: the preceding words act as a case, holding the solution inside them across their word breaks

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of held, all of up and the start of essential

explanation.surface: Swindlers are delayed by vital legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reads as delayed, but the words are only a container for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to trick or deceive them, so the verb form matches cheats.

clue.text: Avoid work making bakery product

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shaped mass of baked bread

explanation.surface: Skiving off by turning out something from the bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means idling instead of working; as a noun it is a whole baked bread item.

clue.text: Newspaper covering latest in cuisine with duck and herb

indicators.note: the newspaper word covers, wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: an organ is a publication that speaks for a group, such as a party newspaper

indicators.note: latest means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: final letter of the word
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A food paper reviewing a duck dish seasoned with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: ORGAN wraps E to make OREGAN, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic Mediterranean plant whose dried leaves season pizza and pasta.

clue.text: Distant church in absurd situation

parts.note: far means distant
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A remote parish church caught up in some ridiculous affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a ridiculous, chaotic event, named after the stage comedy of improbable mishaps.

clue.text: One going into swirling mud's heroic old salt

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the middle of the jumbled letters
swirling means churning round, so the letters are churned into new order

parts.note: Roman numeral one
the thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor wading through churning mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old salt' looks like the sailor, but 'old' is fodder and only 'salt' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Common table salt is chemically this compound, so the chemical name names the salt itself.

clue.text: Sloping surface around hard new frame

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the following word is made over in another order

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
H is the pencil grade for hard
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A joiner's description of a bevelled edge on a fresh frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container indicator, but here it is the abbreviation C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: A chamfer is an angled cut where two faces meet, a bevel planed along an edge.

clue.text: Two thousand in company stop and salute

indicators.note: in company is read as joining the company word, which leads with the thousands following it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, twice
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A firm of two thousand staff halts work to pay tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to praise or honour them publicly, as when you commend their work.

clue.text: United in support for innovator

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
people united are as one

explanation.surface: A team pulling together behind a trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' suggests a football club, but it means ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore or develop something new, an early trailblazer.

clue.text: Monsieur with set of principles about French wine

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the principles word is read backwards

parts.note: a code is a set of rules or principles

explanation.surface: A principled Frenchman holding forth about his country's wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux from the region of that name on the Gironde's left bank.

clue.text: Start development of giant site

indicators.note: development turns land into something different, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Building work begins on an enormous plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something going or bring it about, the transitive sense of start.

clue.text: Still trendy, doctor with edge grew plant yielding essential oil

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even better'
in means fashionable
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain
a rim is an edge
rose means increased

explanation.surface: A fashionable doctor cultivates a plant for its oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'grew' both suggest growth in the surface; they give EVEN and ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant's seeds are pressed for an oil sold as a supplement.

clue.text: Bitter artist with wit stifling exclamation of surprise

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: stifling smothers something by closing round it, so the exclamation sits inside

parts.note: nous is common sense, British slang for wits
cor! is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A resentful painter suppressing a cry of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts; nous and cor! are both everyday British words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of deep-seated resentment and ill will, the same as bitter.

clue.text: Advocate in conclusion less good, lacking weight

parts.note: the end is the conclusion

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the weight abbreviation is left out of the previous word

parts.note: worse is the comparative of bad
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A lawyer's closing argument falls short and carries no weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a noun (a lawyer) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to publicly back or support it, which is what advocating means.

clue.text: Deprived of right to vote since friends had changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are put into an altered order

parts.note: the fifteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lost their vote because their friends changed allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote, so someone stripped of it has been excluded from the electorate.

clue.text: Wrong monarch in decline

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A sinful ruler whose reign is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinking is going down or deteriorating, a figurative match for being on the wane.

clue.text: Sentimental types thus following obligations

parts.note: so means thus
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ties are bonds or obligations

explanation.surface: Soft-hearted people dutifully keeping their commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a position indicator but gives the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Softies are tender-hearted, easily moved people, the informal word for the soft-centred kind.

clue.text: Gesture brought about by a direct love for sculptor

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the gesture word is read backwards

parts.note: a nod is a gesture of the head
taken as written
to tell someone what to do is to direct them
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A gesture of affection prompted by a forthright declaration of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the fifteenth-century Florentine master who made the bronze David.

clue.text: Editor coming up with modest enticement

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means rising from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
coy means shy or modest

explanation.surface: A shy editor making a demure attempt to lure someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy is a lure used to draw a person or animal into a trap, the very thing that entices.

clue.text: Sensational club without boundaries, free

indicators.note: boundaries are the outer edges, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A wild nightclub with no limits and free entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking or vividly graphic, the way a tabloid story is sensational.

clue.text: Unacceptable hesitation in proposal

parts.note: behaviour that is off is unacceptable
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Awkward pauses when someone makes a disappointing proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is something put forward for acceptance, a bid or suggestion of terms.

clue.text: Tale of horror in country around lake and river

indicators.note: the country word goes around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the South American country
L is the abbreviation for lake
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A ghost story set in a South American land by a lake and river.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiller is a frightening story or film designed to send a shiver down the spine.

clue.text: Opening with some soporific effects

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A gaping mouth from the drowsy effects of a sleeping drug.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or mouth-like aperture in the body or an object, so an opening.

clue.text: Turned back with yen for ascetic discipline

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the combined letters read backwards

parts.note: back in time, as in 'years ago'
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Turning away from a craving in favour of self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned back' looks like a single reversal phrase, but 'back' supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga began as a Hindu spiritual practice of self-control and meditation, an austere regime.

clue.text: Separate revolutionary agents infiltrating different side

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so the agents word reads backwards
agents infiltrating get inside, placing one piece within the other
different means changed, so the following word is reordered

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
reps are sales agents

explanation.surface: Rebel spies working their way into the opposing camp.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter in different directions, a verb sense of separating.
